499	    for model, opt, sym in syms:
500	        lines.append(
501	            f' if (model == "{model}" && optimizer == "{opt}")')
502	        lines.append(
503	            f"  return {sym}(ctx, params, input, acts, grad, m, v, extra, sizes,"
504	            " offsets, lr, step, scalars, opt_only, stream);")
505	    lines.append(" *found = false;")
506	    lines.append(" return cudaSuccess;")
507	    lines.append("}")
508	    lines.append("}} // namespace fused::sm90  (within namespace sg)")
509	    return "\n".join(lines)
510	
511	
512	_GFX942_CELL_SIG = (
513	    "PersistentContext, float*, const float*, float*, float*, float*, float*, "
514	    "float*, const int*, const int*, float, int, const FusedScalars&, bool, "
515	    "hipStream_t")
516	
517	
518	def dispatch_table_gfx942() -> str:
519	    """Emit the generated gfx942 fused-cell dispatch table (.inc).
520	
521	    AMD twin of dispatch_table_sm90: declares the 33 gfx942 host launchers
522	    (hipError_t, in sg::fused::gfx942_mega) and dispatch_gfx942_cell(). Compiled
523	    ONLY by a hipcc WITH_HIP build (🟡 MI300X); the WITH_CUDA build #if-excludes
524	    the branch that includes this. Include WITHIN `namespace sg {`.
525	    """
526	    lines: List[str] = []
527	    lines.append("// AUTO-GENERATED by megakernel_codegen.py --dispatch-table-gfx942")
528	    lines.append("// Do not edit by hand. hipcc/WITH_HIP only (🟡 MI300X).")
529	    lines.append("// PersistentContext must already be declared in sg::fused::gfx942_mega.")
530	    lines.append("namespace fused { namespace gfx942_mega {")
531	    syms = []
532	    for plan in mk.solve_all():
533	        if plan.arch != "gfx942":
534	            continue
535	        sym = _cell_symbol(plan.model, plan.optimizer)
536	        syms.append((plan.model, plan.optimizer, sym))
537	        lines.append(f"hipError_t {sym}({_GFX942_CELL_SIG});")
538	    lines.append("")
539	    lines.append("inline hipError_t dispatch_gfx942_cell(")
540	    lines.append(" const std::string& model, const std::string& optimizer,")
541	    lines.append(" PersistentContext ctx, float* params, const float* input,")
542	    lines.append(" float* acts, float* grad, float* m, float* v, float* extra,")
543	    lines.append(" const int* sizes, const int* offsets, float lr, int step,")
544	    lines.append(" const FusedScalars& scalars, bool opt_only,")
545	    lines.append(" hipStream_t stream, bool* found) {")
546	    lines.append(" *found = true;")
547	    for model, opt, sym in syms:
548	        lines.append(f' if (model == "{model}" && optimizer == "{opt}")')
549	        lines.append(
550	            f"  return {sym}(ctx, params, input, acts, grad, m, v, extra, sizes,"
551	            " offsets, lr, step, scalars, opt_only, stream);")
552	    lines.append(" *found = false;")
553	    lines.append(" return hipSuccess;")
554	    lines.append("}")
555	    lines.append("}} // namespace fused::gfx942_mega  (within namespace sg)")
556	    return "\n".join(lines)
557	
558	
559	def dispatch_table() -> str:
560	    """Emit the C++ wired_fused_cell() body covering all 99 cells."""
561	    lines: List[str] = []
562	    lines.append(
563	        "// AUTO-GENERATED by: python -m grokking_optimizers.megakernel_codegen "
564	        "--dispatch-table")
565	    lines.append(
566	        "// Do NOT hand-edit. Derived from the SAME solver enumeration "
567	        "(megakernel.solve_all)")
568	    lines.append(
569	        "// that emits the 99 csrc/fused/<arch>/mega_*.{cu,hip,py} cells, so it "
570	        "cannot drift.")
571	    lines.append("// dispatch.cpp #includes this inside its anonymous namespace.")
572	    lines.append("std::string wired_fused_cell(const std::string& model,")
573	    lines.append(" const std::string& optimizer, int arch) {")
574	    seen: set = set()
575	    for plan in mk.solve_all():
576	        key = (plan.model, plan.optimizer, plan.arch)
577	        if key in seen:
578	            continue
579	        seen.add(key)
580	        tier_tag = _fuse_tier_tag(plan.tier, lower=True)
581	        arch_int = {"sm_90": 90, "gfx942": 942, "tpu_v6e": -1}[plan.arch]
582	        arch_lit = {"sm_90": "sm_90", "gfx942": "gfx942",
583	                    "tpu_v6e": "tpu_v6e"}[plan.arch]
584	        lines.append(
585	            f' if (arch == {arch_int} && model == "{plan.model}"'
586	            f' && optimizer == "{plan.optimizer}")')
587	        lines.append(
588	            f'  return "{tier_tag}:{plan.model}+{plan.optimizer}:{arch_lit}";')
589	    lines.append(' return "";')
590	    lines.append("}")
591	    return "\n".join(lines)
592	
593	
594	# ── CLI ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
595	
596	def main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int:
597	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
598	        prog="megakernel_codegen",
599	        description="Stage 6 L3 megakernel generator (emits per-cell source).")
600	    ap.add_argument("--emit", nargs=3, metavar=("MODEL", "OPTIMIZER", "ARCH"),
601	                    help="emit ONE cell's megakernel source to stdout")
602	    ap.add_argument("--emit-all", action="store_true",
603	                    help="report the full 99-cell manifest with tiers")
604	    ap.add_argument("--write-all", action="store_true",
605	                    help="materialize all 99 cell source files to csrc/fused/")
606	    ap.add_argument("--dispatch-table", action="store_true",
607	                    help="emit the C++ dispatch table covering all 99 cells")
608	    ap.add_argument("--dispatch-table-sm90", action="store_true",
609	                    help="emit the generated sm_90 real-composition dispatch .inc")
610	    ap.add_argument("--dispatch-table-gfx942", action="store_true",
611	                    help="emit the generated gfx942 real-composition dispatch .inc")
612	    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
613	
614	    if args.emit:
615	        model, optimizer, arch = args.emit
616	        try:
617	            sys.stdout.write(emit_cell(model, optimizer, arch))
618	        except (KeyError, RuntimeError) as exc:
619	            sys.stderr.write(f"emit failed: {exc}\n")
620	            return 2
621	        return 0
622	
623	    if args.emit_all:
624	        sys.stdout.write(_format_manifest(manifest()) + "\n")
625	        return 0
626	
627	    if args.write_all:
628	        paths = write_all()
629	        sys.stdout.write(f"Wrote {len(paths)} cell files:\n")
630	        for p in paths:
631	            sys.stdout.write(f"  {p}\n")
632	        return 0
633	
634	    if args.dispatch_table:
635	        sys.stdout.write(dispatch_table() + "\n")
636	        return 0
637	
638	    if args.dispatch_table_sm90:
639	        sys.stdout.write(dispatch_table_sm90() + "\n")
640	        return 0
641	
642	    if args.dispatch_table_gfx942:
643	        sys.stdout.write(dispatch_table_gfx942() + "\n")
644	        return 0
645	
646	    ap.print_help()
647	    return 1
648	
649	
650	if __name__ == "__main__":
651	    raise SystemExit(main())

1	"""grokking_optimizers.megakernel — Stage 6 feasibility solver + generator.
2	
3	Composes the per-arch kernel primitives into one fused **L3 persistent
4	megakernel per (model × optimizer × arch)** — 3 models × 11 optimizers × 3
5	archs = 99 pipelines (§1.5 L3, §1.6 all-99, §1.8 all-three-models).
6	
7	This module is the **automatic feasibility solver** (§1.9/§1.10): it reads each
8	component's register / shared-mem (LDS on AMD) budget from the ARCH_TABLE and
9	picks the highest fusion tier that fits per (model, optimizer, arch); it falls
10	back DOWN tiers when L3 doesn't fit, and **errors** (§1.11 — no silent slow
11	path) when even the lowest tier doesn't fit. The chosen plan is what the C++
12	generator (`csrc/fused/<arch>/`) emits, and what `fused_step` in dispatch.cpp
13	prefers when a fused TU is present (§1.12).
14	
15	Hardware-deferred: the *measured* register counts come from `ptxas
16	-v`/`rocm-llvm` on real silicon; here the solver uses calibrated per-component
17	estimates (recorded in HARDWARE_VALIDATION.md), so the tier selection is
18	🟡 until the on-device register report confirms it.
19	
20	🟡 WORKSTREAM-1 CAVEAT (register-pressure reduction): the component costs below
21	were LOWERED to reflect behavior-preserving SMEM-staging / rematerialization /
22	live-range-shortening in the kernels (model_stages.cuh, supergrok2_sm90.cuh)
23	and the Hopper setmaxnreg producer/consumer warp-group split
24	(fused_megakernel.cuh). The resulting L1→L3/L2 tier promotions are ESTIMATES.
25	ptxas register allocation does NOT match this additive model — it may keep a
26	staged value live anyway, or free a slot we assumed live. The compile.py
27	per-cell `maxrregcount` sweep (knob #1) plus on-silicon `ptxas -v` are the
28	real arbiters; treat every tier change here as 🟡 until silicon confirms it.
29	"""
30	
31	from __future__ import annotations
32	
33	import dataclasses
34	import enum
35	from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
36	
37	from grokking_optimizers.dispatch import canonicalize_model, MODELS, OPTIMIZERS
38	
39	# The ARCH_TABLE (single source of truth for per-arch smem/reg/warp budgets)
40	# lives in compile.py. Import lazily to avoid a heavy import at module load.
41	
42	# The three archs that have hand-written kernel bodies (the megakernel targets).
43	MEGAKERNEL_ARCHS: Tuple[str, ...] = ("sm_90", "gfx942", "tpu_v6e")
44	
45	
46	class FusionTier(enum.IntEnum):
47	    """Fusion tiers, highest (most fused) first. The solver picks the highest
48	    tier whose register + shared-memory footprint fits the arch budget."""
49	    L3_FWD_BWD_OPT = 3   # one persistent kernel: forward + backward + optimizer
50	    L2_BWD_OPT = 2       # backward + optimizer fused; forward separate
51	    L1_OPT_ONLY = 1      # optimizer step fused across params; fwd/bwd separate
52	    L0_UNFUSED = 0       # no fusion (the existing per-op path) — solver ERRORS
53	                         # before returning this for a megakernel request
54	
55	
56	@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
57	class ComponentCost:
58	    """Calibrated per-component resource estimate (one fusion building block).
59	
60	    regs   — registers/thread the component's hot loop needs live.
61	    smem   — bytes of shared memory (LDS on AMD) it stages.
62	    These are the solver inputs; on-silicon `ptxas -v` refines them (🟡).
63	    """
64	    name: str
65	    regs: int
66	    smem: int
67	
68	
69	# ── Calibrated component costs (per model / optimizer) ────────────────────
70	# Forward + backward dominate registers/smem; the optimizer tail is light.
71	# Estimates are deliberately conservative (round up) so the solver never
72	# over-promises a tier that won't fit. Refined from on-device reports (🟡).
73	
74	_MODEL_FWD: Dict[str, ComponentCost] = {
75	    # MFMA/WGMMA attention + FFN: large smem tiles, high reg pressure.
76	    "transformer_decoder": ComponentCost("decoder_fwd", regs=168, smem=49152),
77	    "vit":                 ComponentCost("vit_fwd",     regs=168, smem=49152),
78	    # SSM selective scan: deep recurrence, moderate smem, high regs.
79	    "mamba3":              ComponentCost("mamba3_fwd",  regs=176, smem=40960),
80	}
81	_MODEL_BWD: Dict[str, ComponentCost] = {
82	    # Backward roughly tracks forward + the saved-activation adjoints.
83	    # WORKSTREAM 1 (#2/#3/#4): model_backward_stage now STAGES the upstream
84	    # adjoint slab into shared memory (up_stage[256], +1KB smem) and
85	    # rematerializes x at point-of-use, and model_activation_grad was
86	    # live-range-shortened so u/t/du no longer co-reside. That pulls the
87	    # per-thread live-register working set down from the saved-adjoint estimate.
88	    # 🟡 estimate — ptxas refines on silicon.
89	    "transformer_decoder": ComponentCost("decoder_bwd", regs=168, smem=66560),
90	    "vit":                 ComponentCost("vit_bwd",     regs=168, smem=66560),
91	    "mamba3":              ComponentCost("mamba3_bwd",  regs=176, smem=50176),
92	}
93	# Optimizer-step register/ smem cost (the fused tail). Elementwise optimizers
94	# are cheap; the meta-net optimizers (sg11/15/2) carry a small MLP / attention.
95	_OPT_COST: Dict[str, ComponentCost] = {
96	    "adamw":       ComponentCost("adamw_opt",       regs=40, smem=0),
97	    "lion":        ComponentCost("lion_opt",        regs=32, smem=0),
98	    "grokfast":    ComponentCost("grokfast_opt",    regs=48, smem=0),
99	    "grokadamw":   ComponentCost("grokadamw_opt",   regs=52, smem=0),
100	    "looksam":     ComponentCost("looksam_opt",     regs=56, smem=2048),
101	    "muon":        ComponentCost("muon_opt",        regs=72, smem=4096),
102	    "neuralgrok":  ComponentCost("neuralgrok_opt",  regs=64, smem=1024),
103	    "prodigy":     ComponentCost("prodigy_opt",     regs=56, smem=2048),
104	    "supergrok11": ComponentCost("sg11_opt",        regs=88, smem=4096),
105	    "supergrok15": ComponentCost("sg15_opt",        regs=88, smem=4096),
106	    # SG2's CSA/HCA + PEER meta-net is the heaviest optimizer tail by far.
107	    # WORKSTREAM 1 (#2): the CSA/HCA online-softmax accumulator acc[64] and the
108	    # indexer top-k scratch best_score[64]+best_idx[64] (the dominant per-thread
109	    # register arrays, which spilled to local on real ptxas) are now staged into
110	    # the attention kernels' dynamic shared buffer + a top-k smem scratch. That
111	    # removes ~128 register slots of array state from the hot path; the smem
112	    # rises (acc staging doubles the query buffer, top-k adds block*64*8 B), but
113	    # smem is the near-empty resource. 🟡 estimate.
114	    "supergrok2":  ComponentCost("sg2_opt",         regs=96, smem=49152),
115	}
116	
117	
118	@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
119	class ArchBudget:
120	    name: str
121	    max_regs_per_thread: int
122	    max_smem_per_block: int
123	    warp_size: int
124	    # In a persistent megakernel we pin occupancy; the realistic per-thread
125	    # register ceiling for a 1-CTA-per-SM persistent kernel is the full file.
126	    is_pallas: bool = False
127	
128	
129	def _arch_budget(arch: str) -> ArchBudget:
130	    """Pull the register/smem budget for `arch` from compile.py's ARCH_TABLE."""
131	    from grokking_optimizers.compile import ARCH_TABLE  # lazy
132	    if arch not in ARCH_TABLE:
133	        raise KeyError(f"unknown arch '{arch}' (not in ARCH_TABLE)")
134	    e = ARCH_TABLE[arch]
135	    is_pallas = e.warp_size is None
136	    return ArchBudget(
137	        name=arch,
138	        # Pallas/TPU has no register/smem model exposed here; treat as
139	        # always-fits at the program level (XLA does its own allocation).
140	        max_regs_per_thread=e.max_regs_per_thread or 1 << 30,
141	        max_smem_per_block=e.max_smem_per_block or 1 << 30,
142	        warp_size=e.warp_size or 0,
143	        is_pallas=is_pallas,
144	    )
145	
146	
147	@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
148	class FusionPlan:
149	    model: str
150	    optimizer: str
151	    arch: str
152	    tier: FusionTier
153	    regs: int
154	    smem: int
155	    budget_regs: int
156	    budget_smem: int
157	    note: str = ""
158	
159	    @property
160	    def fits(self) -> bool:
161	        return self.tier > FusionTier.L0_UNFUSED
162	
163	
164	# Hopper setmaxnreg producer-warp-group floor (kProducerRegsF in
165	# fused_megakernel.cuh). The producer WG that runs the light staging + the
166	# optimizer tail is bounded at this allocation; the heavy model stages run on
167	# the consumer WG. See _tier_cost for how the §3.4 split changes the L3 peak.
168	_PRODUCER_WG_REGS = 32
169	
170	
171	def _tier_cost(model: str, optimizer: str,
172	               tier: FusionTier) -> Tuple[int, int]:
173	    """Peak (regs, smem) for a given fusion tier.
174	
175	    WORKSTREAM 1 (#6): the L3 fused kernel now runs as TWO Hopper warp-groups
176	    (setmaxnreg split, fused_megakernel.cuh). The heavy model forward/backward
177	    stages run on the CONSUMER warp-group; the light producer staging + the
178	    optimizer tail run on the PRODUCER warp-group. The SM register *ceiling* a
179	    single warp-group must satisfy is therefore the MAX of the two warp-groups'
180	    footprints, NOT the old sum (max(fwd,bwd) + opt). We bound the consumer WG
181	    by max(fwd,bwd) and the producer WG by the optimizer tail (which subsumes
182	    the producer floor), and take the max. smem is the MAX tile resident at
183	    once (the staged adjoint / attention buffers are summed into the component
184	    smem figures). 🟡 these are MODEL estimates — ptxas register allocation
185	    differs; the per-cell maxrregcount sweep (compile.py knob #1) + on-silicon
186	    `ptxas -v` are the source of truth.
187	    """
188	    fwd = _MODEL_FWD[model]
189	    bwd = _MODEL_BWD[model]
190	    opt = _OPT_COST[optimizer]
191	    if tier == FusionTier.L3_FWD_BWD_OPT:
192	        consumer_wg = max(fwd.regs, bwd.regs)          # heavy model stages
193	        producer_wg = max(opt.regs, _PRODUCER_WG_REGS)  # tail + staging
194	        regs = max(consumer_wg, producer_wg)            # §3.4 split: max, not sum
195	        smem = max(fwd.smem, bwd.smem, opt.smem)
196	    elif tier == FusionTier.L2_BWD_OPT:
197	        regs = bwd.regs + opt.regs
198	        smem = max(bwd.smem, opt.smem)
199	    elif tier == FusionTier.L1_OPT_ONLY:
200	        regs = opt.regs
201	        smem = opt.smem
202	    else:
203	        regs, smem = 0, 0
204	    return regs, smem
205	
206	
207	def solve(model: str, optimizer: str, arch: str) -> FusionPlan:
208	    """§1.9/§1.10 feasibility solver: pick the highest fusion tier that fits.
209	
210	    Falls DOWN tiers when L3 doesn't fit; raises (§1.11 — no silent slow path)
211	    when even L1 (optimizer-only fusion) doesn't fit the arch budget.
212	
213	    Accepts both short names ("mamba", "decoder", "vit") and canonical names
214	    ("mamba3", "transformer_decoder", "vit") via canonicalize_model().
215	    """
216	    model = canonicalize_model(model)
217	    if model not in _MODEL_FWD:
218	        raise KeyError(f"unknown model '{model}'")
219	    if optimizer not in _OPT_COST:
220	        raise KeyError(f"unknown optimizer '{optimizer}'")
221	
222	    b = _arch_budget(arch)
223	
224	    # Pallas/TPU: XLA owns allocation; the megakernel is a single fused program
225	    # and always "fits" at this granularity. Report L3.
226	    if b.is_pallas:
227	        return FusionPlan(model, optimizer, arch, FusionTier.L3_FWD_BWD_OPT,
228	                          regs=0, smem=0, budget_regs=0, budget_smem=0,
229	                          note="pallas/XLA: single fused program, allocator-managed")
230	
231	    for tier in (FusionTier.L3_FWD_BWD_OPT,
232	                 FusionTier.L2_BWD_OPT,
233	                 FusionTier.L1_OPT_ONLY):
234	        regs, smem = _tier_cost(model, optimizer, tier)
235	        if regs <= b.max_regs_per_thread and smem <= b.max_smem_per_block:
236	            note = ""
237	            if tier != FusionTier.L3_FWD_BWD_OPT:
238	                # Record exactly which higher tier(s) busted, and on which
239	                # resource, so the coverage table is self-explaining.
240	                reasons = []
241	                for hi in (FusionTier.L3_FWD_BWD_OPT, FusionTier.L2_BWD_OPT):
242	                    if hi <= tier:
243	                        continue
244	                    hr, hs = _tier_cost(model, optimizer, hi)
245	                    over = []
246	                    if hr > b.max_regs_per_thread:
247	                        over.append(f"regs {hr}>{b.max_regs_per_thread}")
248	                    if hs > b.max_smem_per_block:
249	                        over.append(f"smem {hs}>{b.max_smem_per_block}")
250	                    if over:
251	                        reasons.append(f"{hi.name}({', '.join(over)})")
252	                note = f"fell back to {tier.name}; " + "; ".join(reasons)
253	            return FusionPlan(model, optimizer, arch, tier,
254	                              regs=regs, smem=smem,
255	                              budget_regs=b.max_regs_per_thread,
256	                              budget_smem=b.max_smem_per_block, note=note)
257	
258	    # §1.11: even L1 doesn't fit → hard error, never a silent slow path.
259	    regs, smem = _tier_cost(model, optimizer, FusionTier.L1_OPT_ONLY)
260	    raise RuntimeError(
261	        f"megakernel infeasible for ({model}, {optimizer}, {arch}): even "
262	        f"L1 optimizer-only fusion needs regs={regs}/smem={smem} but the arch "
263	        f"budget is regs={b.max_regs_per_thread}/smem={b.max_smem_per_block}. "
264	        f"No silent slow path (§1.11) — use the unfused per-op dispatch.")
265	
266	
267	def solve_all() -> List[FusionPlan]:
268	    """Solve the full 99-pipeline matrix. Infeasible cells are recorded with an
269	    L0 plan + the reason (so the table is complete) rather than raising, so the
270	    caller can see coverage at a glance."""
271	    plans: List[FusionPlan] = []
272	    for arch in MEGAKERNEL_ARCHS:
273	        for model in MODELS:
274	            for opt in OPTIMIZERS:
275	                try:
276	                    plans.append(solve(model, opt, arch))
277	                except RuntimeError as e:
278	                    b = _arch_budget(arch)
279	                    regs, smem = _tier_cost(model, opt, FusionTier.L1_OPT_ONLY)
280	                    plans.append(FusionPlan(
281	                        model, opt, arch, FusionTier.L0_UNFUSED,
282	                        regs=regs, smem=smem,
283	                        budget_regs=b.max_regs_per_thread,
284	                        budget_smem=b.max_smem_per_block,
285	                        note=f"INFEASIBLE: {e}"))
286	    return plans
287	
288	
289	def coverage_summary() -> Dict[str, int]:
290	    """Tier coverage across all 99 pipelines (for the consolidation report)."""
291	    plans = solve_all()
292	    out: Dict[str, int] = {t.name: 0 for t in FusionTier}
293	    for p in plans:
294	        out[p.tier.name] += 1
295	    return out
296	
297	
298	if __name__ == "__main__":
299	    import json
300	    cov = coverage_summary()
301	    print("Megakernel feasibility-solver coverage (99 pipelines):")
302	    print(json.dumps(cov, indent=2))
303	    # Show any infeasible cells explicitly.
304	    infeasible = [p for p in solve_all() if not p.fits]
305	    if infeasible:
306	        print(f"\n{len(infeasible)} INFEASIBLE cell(s):")
307	        for p in infeasible:
308	            print(f"  ({p.model}, {p.optimizer}, {p.arch}): {p.note}")
309	    else:
310	        print("\nAll 99 pipelines feasible at L1 or higher.")
311

Your approach is right — the task already enumerates the 6 dimensions and the output shape, so don't re-plan. Build the (mechanism × test) matrix first; every other finding hangs off it. Your H3-gap read is correct and confirmed by the source: `test_kernel_matches_reference_gpu` does a real fp64 allclose only for AdamW (line 702-708), the other 10 hit the `isfinite + moved` branch (713-714). But you're about to commit to findings before reading the files where dimensions 2, 4, 5, 6 actually live. Don't declare done until you've read these — they're load-bearing, not skim:

- **verify_all.py, profile_maximal.py** — dimension 2 (gate honesty) is *primarily* here, not in the test files you've read.
- **.github/workflows/ci.yml (66KB)** — grep it, don't read linearly. This decides what actually runs automatically.
- **dispatch.py** (provisional — caveat findings, but the CPU plumbing tests and ABI/build-stamp questions depend on it: `get_ops`, `_opt_scalars_from`, `fused_ready_cells`, `has_fused`).
- **setup.py** — codegen materialization + whether a regenerate-and-diff already exists.
- **tests/hw/decoder_oracle.py, decoder_kernel_mirror.py, test_3d_parallel.py** — in scope ("tests/** all files") and may cover mechanisms you'd otherwise mark uncovered.
- **The 3 shell scripts + a skim of the 11 optimizer .py** — for the "Python-side mechanisms (sam/meta/bilevel/amplifier) have ANY test" sub-question and the dead-path sweep.
- profile.py, utilization.py, megakernel_engine.py — lower priority but in scope.

Specific teeth-checks to run as you go (these change the report's substance — frame each as verify-X):

1. **Does anything auto-run `parity_gate_h100.py`?** It can't be pytest-collected: module-level `assert torch.cuda.is_available()` at line 43 + sections named `section*` not `test_*`. So it only fires if something shells `python tests/hw/parity_gate_h100.py`. Grep verify_all.py and ci.yml for that invocation. If absent: the "recently upgraded SG2 §4 / SG11 §3b" teeth are **manual-runbook-only** — they never bite in automated CI (which is CPU, `-m "not hw"`, so even the AdamW real-allclose is skipped). That's possibly your highest-severity gate-honesty finding.

2. **opt_components.cuh structural check is half-toothed** (check_math line 178-181): it only greps the literal `"csrc/algorithms/adamw.h"`, not all 11, and is guarded by `if fused and` — so a *missing* opt_components.cuh silently skips (the exact bug they hardened the per-op check against at 163-172). A dropped include or reimplemented PEER/GRU/slow math in the fused consumer escapes both this and the re-inline patterns (which only match Adam-moment expressions).

3. **Manifest blind spot — locate lamb_eff.** The task flags "the SG11 lamb_eff change" as bindings-composition. Confirm where lamb_eff actually lives (bindings.cpp / launch_*.py / dispatch.cpp). If it's outside `algorithms/*.h`, the content-hash tooth structurally cannot see it — that's the concrete blind spot to spec a cheap extension for.

4. **SG2 §4b is partially circular.** `expert_out = mu_buf/(1-gru_decay)` is recovered from the kernel's *own* output (line 460), so `mu_new` agrees by construction — the real teeth are only the slow/grokfast term + moments (dm/dv/dslow). The PEER/CSA/HCA routing math is **smoke-only** (4a isfinite, line 404). Document SG2's meta-net forward as NOT numerically covered; only the lamb_eff consumption is. (I traced 3b and 4b — they're non-vacuous given the gate_ok / lamb_ok guards; this circularity is the one caveat.)

For codegen determinism (dim 4): emission order = `solve_all()` = `MEGAKERNEL_ARCHS × MODELS × OPTIMIZERS`. Verify MODELS/OPTIMIZERS in dispatch.py are ordered (list/tuple, not set) before you bless determinism, and check setup.py/ci.yml for an existing regenerate-and-diff before spec'ing one.

None of this blocks the approach — it's the content you still need to gather. The two things that would make the report *wrong*: blessing the SG2/SG11 upgrades as "real teeth" without (1) noting nothing auto-runs them and (4) the §4b mu circularity. Nail those.

1	"""End-to-end verification harness — the single authoritative gate for
2	SuperGrok1.5.  "Know EVERYTHING; prove it works, and works *maximally*."
3	
4	This is the end-all-be-all.  It does not just check that individual files
5	compile in isolation — it proves that the **modular composition** works: every
6	optimizer compiles *together with* every model into the fused megakernel cell
7	for every arch (99 cells), and that each composition runs at its **maximal**
8	fusion tier.  It then cross-validates the generated artifacts against their
9	single source of truth so nothing can silently drift.
10	
11	It is organized as ordered phases; each phase prints one PASS/FAIL line per
12	check and accumulates into a final structured report.  Phases that need a tool
13	absent on this host (nvcc / clang / jax) are reported as SKIPPED-silicon rather
14	than silently passing.
15	
16	    PHASE 0  toolchain probe            — what can be proven here vs on silicon
17	    PHASE 1  structural inventory       — every component + 99 cells exist
18	    PHASE 2  single-component gates      — per-op launchers + models + headers
19	    PHASE 3  MODULAR COMPOSITION         — 99 cells: optimizer × model compile
20	                                            *together* (the core guarantee)
21	    PHASE 4  MAXIMALITY                   — max fusion tier, codegen idempotency,
22	                                            register/smem budget, math drift
23	    PHASE 5  cross-validation            — dispatch tables, self-test, ruff
24	    PHASE 6  report                       — totals + tier map + silicon + design
25	
26	Run:
27	    PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m grokking_optimizers.verify_all              # all
28	    PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m grokking_optimizers.verify_all --phase 3    # one
29	    PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m grokking_optimizers.verify_all --quick      # no compiles
30	    PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m grokking_optimizers.verify_all --jobs 8     # parallelism
31	
32	Failure policy mirrors utilization.py: a missing *expected* artifact or a failed
33	*runnable* check is a hard FAIL.  A check that genuinely needs an accelerator is
34	SKIPPED-silicon and listed at the end — never a false green.
35	"""
36	
37	from __future__ import annotations
38	
39	import argparse
40	import concurrent.futures
41	import dataclasses
42	import os
43	import re
44	import shutil
45	import subprocess
46	import sys
47	import threading
48	import time
49	from pathlib import Path
50	from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
51	
52	REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
53	
54	from grokking_optimizers import megakernel as mk
55	from grokking_optimizers import megakernel_codegen as cg
56	
57	OPTIMIZERS: Tuple[str, ...] = mk.OPTIMIZERS
58	MODELS: Tuple[str, ...] = mk.MODELS
59	ARCHES: Tuple[str, ...] = mk.MEGAKERNEL_ARCHS  # sm_90, gfx942, tpu_v6e
60	N_CELLS = len(OPTIMIZERS) * len(MODELS) * len(ARCHES)  # 99
61	
62	
63	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
64	# Result records
65	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
66	
67	PASS, FAIL, SKIP = "PASS", "FAIL", "SKIP-silicon"
68	
69	
70	@dataclasses.dataclass
71	class Check:
72	    phase: str
73	    name: str
74	    status: str            # PASS | FAIL | SKIP-silicon
75	    detail: str = ""
76	    seconds: float = 0.0
77	
78	
79	class Report:
80	    def __init__(self) -> None:
81	        self.checks: List[Check] = []
82	        self.tier_map: Dict[str, Dict[str, int]] = {}
83	        self.silicon: List[str] = []
84	        self.design: List[str] = []
85	
86	    def add(self, c: Check) -> Check:
87	        self.checks.append(c)
88	        glyph = {"PASS": "PASS ", "FAIL": "FAIL ",
89	                 "SKIP-silicon": "SKIP "}[c.status]
90	        tail = f"  ({c.seconds:.1f}s)" if c.seconds >= 0.1 else ""
91	        line = f"  {glyph} [{c.phase}] {c.name}{tail}"
92	        if c.detail and c.status != PASS:
93	            line += f"\n         {c.detail}"
94	        sys.stdout.write(line + "\n")
95	        sys.stdout.flush()
96	        return c
97	
98	    def count(self, status: str, phase: Optional[str] = None) -> int:
99	        return sum(1 for c in self.checks
100	                   if c.status == status and (phase is None or c.phase == phase))
101	
102

104	# Toolchain probe
105	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
106

135	
136	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
137	# Shell helpers
138	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
139	
140	# A CUTLASS-heavy nvcc compile can OOM when several run concurrently (SIGKILL →
141	# rc -9 / 137). That is memory contention, NOT a compile error — the TU builds
142	# fine alone. When we see a kill we retry the unit ONCE while holding this lock,
143	# so the retry runs with the machine to itself.
144	_EXCLUSIVE = threading.Lock()
145	
146	
147	def _is_oom_kill(rc: int, out: str) -> bool:
148	    # SIGKILL is the authoritative signal (rc -9 / 137). The end-of-output
149	    # "Killed" line is the kernel's OOM-killer message. An UNANCHORED
150	    # `"Killed" in out` would misclassify a deterministic compile error whose
151	    # diagnostic merely contains the word "Killed" as a transient OOM, masking
152	    # a real failure as flaky — so only trust the rc and the end-of-output tag.
153	    return rc in (-9, 137) or out.strip().endswith("Killed")
154	
155	
156	def _run(cmd: List[str], timeout: int = 300) -> Tuple[int, str]:
157	    """Run a command in REPO_ROOT, return (rc, combined-tail)."""
158	    proc = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=str(REPO_ROOT), capture_output=True,
159	                          text=True, timeout=timeout)
160	    out = (proc.stdout or "") + (proc.stderr or "")
161	    return proc.returncode, out.strip()
162	
163	
164	def _run_resilient(cmd: List[str], timeout: int = 600) -> Tuple[int, str]:
165	    """_run, but if the child is OOM-killed, retry once holding _EXCLUSIVE so
166	    the heavy compile runs alone (full memory)."""
167	    rc, out = _run(cmd, timeout)
168	    if _is_oom_kill(rc, out):
169	        with _EXCLUSIVE:
170	            rc, out = _run(cmd, timeout)
171	    return rc, out

304	def _nvcc_compile(tu: Path) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
305	    # -DWITH_CUTLASS is the MAXIMAL sm_90 build config (the shipped fast path:
306	    # CUTLASS WGMMA/TMA collectives for SG2 + the model GEMMs). supergrok2's
307	    # launcher and the model TUs hard-#error without it; the cuBLAS megakernel
308	    # cells are unaffected by it. Test what actually ships.
309	    rc, out = _run_resilient(
310	        ["bash", "scripts/compile_to_object.sh", str(tu), "-DWITH_CUTLASS"],
311	        timeout=900)

313	        return True, ""

315	        return False, "OOM-killed even on exclusive retry (lower --jobs)"
316	    return False, _first_error(out)

338	def _parallel_compile(rep: Report, phase: str, label: str, units: List[Path],
339	                      fn: Callable[[Path], Tuple[bool, str]], jobs: int) -> None:
340	    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=jobs) as ex:
341	        futs = {ex.submit(_timed, fn, u): u for u in units}
342	        for fut in concurrent.futures.as_completed(futs):
343	            u = futs[fut]
344	            ok, detail, secs = fut.result()
345	            rep.add(Check(phase, f"{label} {u.stem}",
346	                          PASS if ok else FAIL, detail, secs))
347	
348	
349	def _timed(fn: Callable[[Path], Tuple[bool, str]], u: Path
350	           ) -> Tuple[bool, str, float]:
351	    t0 = time.monotonic()
352	    ok, detail = fn(u)
353	    return ok, detail, time.monotonic() - t0

356	def _tpu_trace_all(rep: Report, jobs: int) -> None:
357	    """Trace+lower every tpu_v6e fused cell via its verify() (CPU jax)."""
358	    import importlib
359	
360	    def one(model: str, opt: str) -> Tuple[bool, str, float]:
361	        t0 = time.monotonic()
362	        mod_name = f"csrc.fused.tpu_v6e.mega_{model}_{opt}"
363	        try:
364	            mod = importlib.import_module(mod_name)
365	            importlib.reload(mod)
366	            mod.verify()
367	            return True, "", time.monotonic() - t0
368	        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — surface the trace failure
369	            return False, f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"[:200], \
370	                time.monotonic() - t0
371	
372	    cells = [(m, o) for m in MODELS for o in OPTIMIZERS]
373	    # jax tracing is not thread-safe across reloads; keep TPU trace serial-ish.
374	    workers = max(1, min(jobs, 4))
375	    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=workers) as ex:
376	        futs = {ex.submit(one, m, o): (m, o) for m, o in cells}
377	        for fut in concurrent.futures.as_completed(futs):
378	            m, o = futs[fut]
379	            ok, detail, secs = fut.result()
380	            rep.add(Check("3", f"tpu_v6e compose mega_{m}_{o}",
381	                          PASS if ok else FAIL, detail, secs))

388	def phase4_maximality(rep: Report) -> None:
389	    sys.stdout.write("\n[PHASE 4] MAXIMALITY — max fusion tier, idempotency, "
390	                     "budget, single-source\n")
391	
392	    plans = mk.solve_all()
393	    by_arch_tier: Dict[str, Dict[str, int]] = {a: {} for a in ARCHES}
394	
395	    # 4a. Every cell is FEASIBLE (>= L1) — no infeasible compositions.
396	    infeasible = [p for p in plans if not p.fits]
397	    rep.add(Check("4", f"all {N_CELLS} cells feasible (≥L1)",
398	                  PASS if not infeasible else FAIL,
399	                  "" if not infeasible
400	                  else f"{len(infeasible)} infeasible: "
401	                       f"{[(p.model, p.optimizer, p.arch) for p in infeasible][:3]}"))
402	
403	    # 4b. Every cell sits at the MAX tier that fits its budget (the solver's
404	    # job — re-derive independently and confirm no cell could go higher).
405	    not_maximal: List[str] = []
406	    for p in plans:
407	        tier = p.tier
408	        by_arch_tier[p.arch][tier.name] = \
409	            by_arch_tier[p.arch].get(tier.name, 0) + 1
410	        if p.arch == "tpu_v6e":
411	            continue  # XLA-managed; solver reports L3 by construction.
412	        b = mk._arch_budget(p.arch)
413	        # Could a strictly higher tier have fit? If so, the solver under-fused.
414	        for higher in (mk.FusionTier.L3_FWD_BWD_OPT, mk.FusionTier.L2_BWD_OPT):
415	            if higher <= tier:
416	                continue
417	            hr, hs = mk._tier_cost(p.model, p.optimizer, higher)
418	            if hr <= b.max_regs_per_thread and hs <= b.max_smem_per_block:
419	                not_maximal.append(
420	                    f"{p.model}/{p.optimizer}/{p.arch}: at {tier.name} but "
421	                    f"{higher.name} fits ({hr}r/{hs}s)")
422	    rep.add(Check("4", "every cell at its MAX feasible tier",
423	                  PASS if not not_maximal else FAIL,
424	                  "" if not not_maximal else "; ".join(not_maximal[:3])))
425	    rep.tier_map = by_arch_tier
426	
427	    # 4c. Each cell within the arch register + smem budget at its chosen tier.
428	    over_budget: List[str] = []
429	    for p in plans:
430	        if p.arch == "tpu_v6e":
431	            continue
432	        b = mk._arch_budget(p.arch)
433	        if p.regs > b.max_regs_per_thread or p.smem > b.max_smem_per_block:
434	            over_budget.append(
435	                f"{p.model}/{p.optimizer}/{p.arch}: {p.regs}r/{p.smem}s "
436	                f"> {b.max_regs_per_thread}r/{b.max_smem_per_block}s")
437	    rep.add(Check("4", "every cell within register+smem budget",
438	                  PASS if not over_budget else FAIL,
439	                  "" if not over_budget else "; ".join(over_budget[:3])))
440	
441	    # 4d. CODEGEN IDEMPOTENCY: re-emit every cell in memory and assert it is
442	    # byte-identical to the committed file (no drift, no stale generated code).
443	    drifted: List[str] = []
444	    for p in plans:
445	        path = _cell_path(p.model, p.optimizer, p.arch)
446	        if not path.exists():
447	            drifted.append(f"{path.name} (missing)")
448	            continue
449	        emitted = cg.emit_cell(p.model, p.optimizer, p.arch)
450	        if emitted.rstrip() != path.read_text().rstrip():
451	            drifted.append(path.name)
452	    rep.add(Check("4", f"codegen idempotency ({N_CELLS} cells byte-identical)",
453	                  PASS if not drifted else FAIL,
454	                  "" if not drifted
455	                  else f"{len(drifted)} drifted: {drifted[:5]}"))
456	
457	    # 4e. The committed cell's tier COMMENT matches the solver's live decision
458	    # (catches a stale generated header even if the body is right).
459	    tier_mismatch: List[str] = []
460	    for p in plans:
461	        path = _cell_path(p.model, p.optimizer, p.arch)
462	        if not path.exists():
463	            continue
464	        head = path.read_text()[:400]
465	        if p.tier.name not in head and _short_tier(p.tier) not in head:
466	            tier_mismatch.append(f"{path.name} (want {p.tier.name})")
467	    rep.add(Check("4", "cell tier-comment matches solver",
468	                  PASS if not tier_mismatch else FAIL,
469	                  "" if not tier_mismatch else f"{tier_mismatch[:5]}"))
470	
471	    # 4f. Math single-source drift guard (the optimizer math is shared between
472	    # per-op and fused paths — maximal reuse, zero divergence).
473	    rc, out = _run([sys.executable, "scripts/check_math_single_source.py"],
474	                   timeout=120)
475	    rep.add(Check("4", "optimizer-math single-source drift guard",
476	                  PASS if rc == 0 else FAIL,
477	                  "" if rc == 0 else _first_error(out)))
478

489	def phase5_crossval(rep: Report, tc: Toolchain) -> None:
490	    sys.stdout.write("\n[PHASE 5] cross-validation — generated artifacts vs "
491	                     "single source\n")
492	
493	    # 5a. The three dispatch tables match their generators byte-for-byte.
494	    pairs = [
495	        ("sm_90 dispatch table", "csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_dispatch_table.inc",
496	         cg.dispatch_table_sm90),
497	        ("gfx942 dispatch table", "csrc/fused/gfx942/fused_dispatch_table.inc",
498	         cg.dispatch_table_gfx942),
499	        ("wired_fused_cells", "csrc/fused/fused_wired_cells.inc",
500	         cg.dispatch_table),
501	    ]
502	    for label, path, gen in pairs:
503	        committed = (REPO_ROOT / path).read_text()
504	        rep.add(Check("5", label,
505	                      PASS if gen().rstrip() == committed.rstrip() else FAIL,
506	                      "" if gen().rstrip() == committed.rstrip()
507	                      else "generator output differs from committed file"))
508	
509	    # 5b. fused_wired_cells routes every (arch,model,opt) the solver knows and
510	    # carries no stale tpu_v5p.
511	    wired = (REPO_ROOT / "csrc/fused/fused_wired_cells.inc").read_text()
512	    rep.add(Check("5", "no stale tpu_v5p in active dispatch",
513	                  PASS if "tpu_v5p" not in wired else FAIL))
514	    # Check the ACTUAL per-pair route literal for each GPU arch the wired
515	    # function dispatches (sm_90 + gfx942; TPU is dispatched separately). The
516	    # old check used `+{o}: in wired or '"{m}' in wired and {m}+{o} in wired`,
517	    # whose `A or (B and C)` form (with A/B near-always False because every
518	    # opt/model appears under *some* pair) could not detect a specific
519	    # (model,opt) route being dropped — a reproduced false-green. The route
520	    # literals look like "l3:transformer_decoder+adamw:sm_90".
521	    _GPU_ARCH_SUFFIXES = ("sm_90", "gfx942")
522	    route_miss = [f"{m}+{o}:{suf}"
523	                  for m in MODELS for o in OPTIMIZERS
524	                  for suf in _GPU_ARCH_SUFFIXES
525	                  if f"{m}+{o}:{suf}" not in wired]
526	    rep.add(Check("5", "wired table routes all model+opt pairs",
527	                  PASS if not route_miss else FAIL,
528	                  "" if not route_miss else f"{route_miss[:5]}"))
529	
530	    # 5c. Self-test suite (authoritative count guard inside compile.py).
531	    rc, out = _run([sys.executable, "-m", "grokking_optimizers.compile",
532	                    "--self-test"], timeout=600)
533	    # Match the real summary line: `"0 failed"` as a substring also matches
534	    # "10 failed"/"20 failed"/etc., so anchor on the full "N passed, 0 failed".
535	    ok = rc == 0 and bool(re.search(r"\b[1-9][0-9]* passed, 0 failed\b", out))
536	    summary = next((ln for ln in out.splitlines()
537	                    if "passed," in ln and "failed" in ln), "")
538	    rep.add(Check("5", "compile.py --self-test",
539	                  PASS if ok else FAIL, summary.strip()))
540	
541	    # 5d. ruff lint clean across the package + scripts.
542	    if shutil.which("ruff"):
543	        rc, out = _run(["ruff", "check", "grokking_optimizers/", "scripts/"],
544	                       timeout=120)
545	        rep.add(Check("5", "ruff lint clean",
546	                      PASS if rc == 0 else FAIL,
547	                      "" if rc == 0 else _first_error(out)))
548	    else:
549	        rep.add(Check("5", "ruff lint", SKIP, "ruff absent"))
550	
551	    # 5e. utilization crash-hard contract still holds (no device here → raises).
552	    try:
553	        from grokking_optimizers import utilization as u
554	        raised = False
555	        try:
556	            u.track_cell("adamw", "mamba", "sm_90a", iters=1, timeout=10)
557	        except RuntimeError:
558	            raised = True
559	        rep.add(Check("5", "utilization crash-hard (raises w/o device)",
560	                      PASS if raised else FAIL,
561	                      "" if raised else "track_cell did not raise"))
562	    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
563	        rep.add(Check("5", "utilization crash-hard", FAIL, str(exc)[:200]))

649	def main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int:
650	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
651	        prog="python -m grokking_optimizers.verify_all",
652	        description="End-all-be-all verification: prove the modular "
653	                    "composition compiles AND runs maximally across all 99 "
654	                    "fused pipelines.")

656	                    help="Run only one phase (default: all).")

658	                    help="Skip the compile-heavy phases 2+3 (inventory + "
659	                         "maximality + cross-val only).")
660	    ap.add_argument("--jobs", "-j", type=int, default=os.cpu_count() or 4,
661	                    help="Parallel compile workers (default: ncpu).")
662	    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

664	    started = time.monotonic()
665	    tc = probe_toolchain()
666	    sys.stdout.write("[PHASE 0] toolchain probe\n")
667	    sys.stdout.write(
668	        f"  nvcc={'yes' if tc.nvcc else 'NO'}  "
669	        f"clang={'yes' if tc.clang else 'NO'}  "
670	        f"jax={'yes' if tc.has_jax else 'NO'}  "
671	        f"gpu={'yes' if tc.has_gpu else 'NO'}  "

4	(every cell at its max feasible fusion tier).  This module goes one level deeper:
5	it inspects the **actual emitted machine code** to prove the binaries do what we
6	want *maximally* — the compute-bound paths use the silicon's tensor cores, the
7	async-copy engines, and don't spill registers — and that the optimizer math

147	#   `vit_run_gemm_atb<float>` (grokking_optimizers/kernels/sm_90/vit_sm90.cuh
148	#   ~L489). Its `if constexpr (std::is_same<T, float>::value)` branch does NOT
149	#   call CUTLASS — it returns `cudaErrorNotSupported`, so the ViT float wgrad
150	#   falls back to the scalar `gemm_grad_weight_kernel`. The TF32 RS collective
151	#   is *deliberately* routed to scalar because CUTLASS 3.x fails a HARD
152	#   static_assert for it ("SmemLayoutB K must be 128bytes to be transposed"):
153	#   see the DOCUMENT-STOP in csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/mma.cuh (~L720-740). The
154	#   LIVE TF32 model GEMMs use the SS path instead (`Sm90GemmBT<tfloat32_t>`,
155	#   `MMA_64x128x8_F32TF32TF32_SS_TN`, `MainloopSm90TmaGmmaWarpSpecialized`),
156	#   which has 0 spills. So this kernel body is *emitted but never launched*.
157	#
158	# WHY maxrregcount DOES NOT FIX IT: the kernel uses 168/255 registers, so a
159	#   higher register ceiling is non-binding — `-Xptxas --maxrregcount` at 192
160	#   AND 255 was tested on-silicon and did NOT clear the 8 B spill. The spill is
161	#   intrinsic to this dead RS mainloop's codegen, not a register-pressure knob.
162	#
163	# The match below requires ALL THREE tokens that are UNIQUE to the RS kernel
164	# (the `_RS_` atom + the `RmemA` collective + the element type). The live SS
165	# kernel in the SAME TU also contains `MMA_64x128x8` and `tfloat32_t`, so those
166	# two alone are NOT sufficient — the `_RS_TN` / `RmemAWarpSpecialized` tokens
167	# are what separate this single dead kernel from every live one. All three are
168	# literal substrings of the ptxas mangled name (verified on H100/CUDA 12.4), so
169	# we match the raw mangled string with no runtime c++filt. The check is
170	# FAIL-CLOSED: ANY spilling kernel that does not match ALL THREE still FAILs.
171	_DEAD_SPILL_KERNEL_TOKENS: Tuple[str, ...] = (
172	    "MMA_64x128x8_F32TF32TF32_RS_TN",        # the RS (register-source) TF32 atom
173	    "MainloopSm90TmaGmmaRmemAWarpSpecialized",  # the RmemA collective (RS path)
174	    "tfloat32_t",                            # element type (FP32 → TF32 MMA)
175	)
176	_DEAD_SPILL_NOTE = (
177	    "ALLOWED: known dead-code CUTLASS TF32-RS GEMM "
178	    "(MMA_64x128x8_F32TF32TF32_RS_TN / MainloopSm90TmaGmmaRmemAWarpSpecialized), "
179	    "8B spill, runtime-unreachable via vit_run_gemm_atb<float> scalar fallback "
180	    "— see mma.cuh DOCUMENT-STOP (maxrregcount does not clear it: 168/255 regs)"
181	)
182	
183	
184	def _is_dead_spill_kernel(mangled: str) -> bool:
185	    """True iff `mangled` is THE single allowlisted dead-code CUTLASS TF32-RS
186	    kernel (matches ALL of the RS-unique tokens). Fail-closed: any other
187	    spilling kernel returns False and therefore still FAILs the spill check."""
188	    return all(tok in mangled for tok in _DEAD_SPILL_KERNEL_TOKENS)
189	
190	
191	# Self-check (runs at import): the allowlist must accept the dead RS kernel and
192	# REJECT the live SS kernel that shares the MMA_64x128x8 / tfloat32_t tokens, so
193	# the exception can never widen into a category relax. Both are real ptxas
194	# mangled names captured from the model TUs on sm_90.
195	assert _is_dead_spill_kernel(
196	    "_ZN7cutlass13device_kernel...MainloopSm90TmaGmmaRmemAWarpSpecialized..."
197	    "tfloat32_t...MMA_64x128x8_F32TF32TF32_RS_TN..."), \
198	    "allowlist must accept the dead TF32-RS kernel"
199	assert not _is_dead_spill_kernel(
200	    "_ZN7cutlass13device_kernel...MainloopSm90TmaGmmaWarpSpecialized..."
201	    "tfloat32_t...MMA_64x128x8_F32TF32TF32_SS_TN..."), \
202	    "allowlist must REJECT the live TF32-SS kernel (no _RS_/RmemA tokens)"
203

205	@dataclasses.dataclass
206	class SassProfile:
207	    rc: int
208	    regs_max: int
209	    smem_max: int
210	    spill_bytes: int             # max spill across ALL kernels (for display)
211	    unexpected_spill_bytes: int  # max spill across NON-allowlisted kernels (gate)
212	    allowed_spill: bool          # the dead-code TF32-RS spiller was present
213	    c7509: int           # wgmma-serialization warnings
214	    wgmma: int
215	    tma: int
216	    mbarrier: int
217	    mufu: int
218	    ffma: int
219	    log: str
220	
221	
222	# Per-kernel ptxas-v block: "Function properties for <MANGLED>\n  <stack> bytes
223	# stack frame, <spill> bytes spill stores, ...". This pairs every spill byte
224	# count with the EXACT kernel it belongs to (verified exhaustive: every spill
225	# line in the model TUs is immediately preceded by its Function-properties line).
226	_PTXAS_SPILL_BLOCK = re.compile(
227	    r"Function properties for (\S+)\s*\n"
228	    r"\s*\d+ bytes stack frame, (\d+) bytes spill stores")
229	
230	
231	def _nvcc_profile(tu: Path, timeout: int = 900) -> SassProfile:
232	    """Compile a sm_90 TU with the maximal flags + ptxas -v, then SASS-audit."""
233	    obj = Path(tempfile.mktemp(suffix=".o"))
234	    cmd = ["nvcc", *_MAX_NVCC, *_torch_incs(), "-Xptxas", "-v",
235	           str(tu), "-o", str(obj)]
236	    proc = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=str(REPO_ROOT), capture_output=True,
237	                          text=True, timeout=timeout)
238	    log = (proc.stdout or "") + (proc.stderr or "")
239	    regs = [int(m) for m in re.findall(r"Used (\d+) registers", log)]
240	    smem = [int(m) for m in re.findall(r"(\d+) bytes smem", log)]
241	    spills = [int(m) for m in re.findall(r"(\d+) bytes spill stores", log)]
242	    # Attribute each spill to its kernel so the allowlist is per-kernel, not
243	    # per-TU: an allowlisted dead kernel does not absolve a real spiller in the
244	    # same TU. unexpected_spill_bytes is the gate; spill_bytes stays the raw max.
245	    unexpected = 0
246	    allowed_spill = False
247	    for mangled, sb in _PTXAS_SPILL_BLOCK.findall(log):
248	        nbytes = int(sb)
249	        if nbytes == 0:
250	            continue
251	        if _is_dead_spill_kernel(mangled):
252	            allowed_spill = True
253	        else:
254	            unexpected = max(unexpected, nbytes)
255	    c7509 = len(re.findall(r"C7509", log))
256	    wgmma = tma = mbar = mufu = ffma = 0
257	    if proc.returncode == 0 and obj.exists():
258	        sass = subprocess.run(["cuobjdump", "-sass", str(obj)],
259	                              capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
260	        wgmma = len(re.findall(r"\b[HUW]?GMMA\b", sass))
261	        tma = len(re.findall(r"UTMALDG|UBLKCP|cp\.async\.bulk", sass))
262	        mbar = len(re.findall(r"MBARRIER|ELECT|ARRIVES", sass))
263	        mufu = len(re.findall(r"MUFU", sass))
264	        ffma = len(re.findall(r"\bFFMA\b", sass))
265	        obj.unlink(missing_ok=True)
266	    return SassProfile(
267	        proc.returncode, max(regs, default=0), max(smem, default=0),
268	        max(spills, default=0), unexpected, allowed_spill,
269	        c7509, wgmma, tma, mbar, mufu, ffma, log)

484	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
485	
486	def tier_d_functional(rep: Report) -> None:
487	    sys.stdout.write("\n[TIER D] functional correctness — the optimizer math "
488	                     "ACTUALLY optimizes (CPU execution)\n")
489	    try:
490	        import jax  # noqa: F401
491	        import jax.numpy as jnp
492	    except Exception:
493	        rep.add(Probe("D", "optimizer descent (jax CPU)", SKIP, "jax absent"))
494	        rep.silicon.append("functional optimizer execution (needs jax)")
495	        return
496	
497	    # Pure-jax reference of each optimizer's per-element step would duplicate
498	    # csrc/algorithms; instead drive the real per-element math the canonical
499	    # headers encode, via a minimal convex problem: minimise f(w)=||w-t||^2.
500	    # A correct optimizer must (a) strictly reduce the loss over N steps and
501	    # (b) keep every iterate finite. We test the Adam-family update (the shared
502	    # core of 8/11 optimizers) and Lion (sign-based) as representatives.
503	    import jax
504	
505	    def adam_descent() -> Tuple[bool, str]:
506	        w = jnp.array([5.0, -3.0, 1.0])
507	        t = jnp.array([1.0, 1.0, 1.0])
508	        m = jnp.zeros(3)
509	        v = jnp.zeros(3)
510	        b1, b2, eps, lr = 0.9, 0.999, 1e-8, 0.1
511	        loss0 = float(jnp.sum((w - t) ** 2))
512	        for step in range(1, 201):
513	            g = 2.0 * (w - t)
514	            m = b1 * m + (1 - b1) * g
515	            v = b2 * v + (1 - b2) * g * g
516	            mh = m / (1 - b1 ** step)
517	            vh = v / (1 - b2 ** step)
518	            w = w - lr * mh / (jnp.sqrt(vh) + eps)
519	            if not bool(jnp.all(jnp.isfinite(w))):
520	                return False, f"non-finite iterate at step {step}"
521	        loss1 = float(jnp.sum((w - t) ** 2))
522	        ok = loss1 < loss0 * 1e-3
523	        return ok, f"loss {loss0:.3f} -> {loss1:.2e} (Adam core, 200 steps)"
524	
525	    def lion_descent() -> Tuple[bool, str]:
526	        w = jnp.array([5.0, -3.0, 1.0])
527	        t = jnp.array([1.0, 1.0, 1.0])
528	        m = jnp.zeros(3)
529	        b1, b2, lr = 0.9, 0.99, 0.05
530	        loss0 = float(jnp.sum((w - t) ** 2))
531	        for _ in range(400):
532	            g = 2.0 * (w - t)
533	            update = jnp.sign(b1 * m + (1 - b1) * g)
534	            w = w - lr * update
535	            m = b2 * m + (1 - b2) * g
536	            if not bool(jnp.all(jnp.isfinite(w))):
537	                return False, "non-finite iterate"
538	        loss1 = float(jnp.sum((w - t) ** 2))
539	        return loss1 < loss0, f"loss {loss0:.3f} -> {loss1:.3e} (Lion, 400 steps)"
540	
541	    for name, fn in (("Adam-family core descent", adam_descent),
542	                     ("Lion sign-update descent", lion_descent)):
543	        t0 = time.monotonic()
544	        ok, detail = fn()
545	        rep.add(Probe("D", name, PASS if ok else FAIL, detail,
546	                      time.monotonic() - t0))
547	
548	    # Also confirm a real fused (model, optimizer) Pallas program TRACES,
549	    # LOWERS, and is invocable on CPU — the binary path executes end to end.
550	    try:
551	        from csrc.backends.pallas._pallas_fused import trace_check
552	        r = trace_check("mamba3", "adamw", "L3")
553	        rep.add(Probe("D", "fused mamba3/adamw program lowers (CPU)",
554	                      PASS if r else FAIL, f"trace_check -> {r!r}"))
555	    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
556	        rep.add(Probe("D", "fused program lowers", FAIL, str(exc)[:160]))

561	# host execution (the TPU analogue of the SASS/ISA audit — the MXU is XLA-

6	  the REAL transformer-decoder fwd+bwd. That CUDA backward is hand-derived and
7	  the implementing agent cannot compile or run it. So we first write the SAME
8	  fwd+bwd here in plain PyTorch using ONLY primitive ops — and a MANUAL backward
9	  (NO autograd) — then assert it matches torch.autograd's loss and every
10	  parameter .grad to ~1e-6. The CUDA megakernel is then ported line-for-line from
11	  this verified reference, converting "is my hand-derived backward correct?"
12	  (unrunnable) into "does my manual Python match autograd?" (runnable now).
13	
14	  This module is ALSO the per-tensor expected-grad oracle the parity test
15	  (tests/hw/test_megakernel_vs_eager.py, item 5a) consumes: same init, same

19	  Transformer(nl=2, d=128, h=4, ntok=99, seq=4)  [_raw_model hardcodes seq=4]

21	    pos = Embedding(4, 128)             # seq=4 positions

24	             causal mask = triu(ones(seq,seq), diagonal=1)            # :352
25	      n1, n2 = LayerNorm(128)           # :350  (eps=1e-5 default)
26	      ff = Linear(128,512) → GELU → Linear(512,128)   # :351 (GELU = exact erf)
27	      forward: a,_ = attn(x,x,x, attn_mask=causal)    # :354
28	               x = n1(x + a)                          # :355 POST-LN
29	               return n2(x + ff(x))                   # :355 POST-LN
30	    norm = LayerNorm(128)              # :362  final LN
31	    out  = Linear(128, 99)            # :362  head → 99 logits
32	    forward: h = tok(x) + pos(pos_ids)                # :366
33	             for l in layers: h = l(h)                # :367
34	             return out(norm(h)[:, -1, :])            # :368  LAST token only

37	  nn.MultiheadAttention internals (verified bit-identical to the manual form in
38	  this file, max|diff|==0): in_proj_weight [3d, d] packs [Wq; Wk; Wv] row-blocks,
39	  in_proj_bias [3d]; qkv = x @ W_in^T + b_in then split into q,k,v each [.,.,d];
40	  per-head dh = d/h = 32; scores = (qh @ kh^T)/sqrt(dh); causal-masked (-inf on
41	  j>i); softmax over the key axis; ctx = attn @ vh; merge heads; out = ctx @
42	  W_out^T + b_out  (out_proj.weight [d,d], out_proj.bias [d]).
43	
44	NUMERICS (each verified against autograd here, and the values the CUDA must use):
45	  * GELU = EXACT erf: 0.5*x*(1+erf(x/sqrt2)); derivative
46	    0.5*(1+erf(x/sqrt2)) + x * (1/sqrt(2*pi)) * exp(-x^2/2).
47	    (The surrogate's tanh approximation differs by ~4e-4 — blows the 1e-4 grad
48	    tolerance — so it is WRONG for this path.)
49	  * LayerNorm eps = 1e-5 (torch default). Backward dx uses the two
50	    mean-correction terms (see _layernorm_backward).
51	  * Attention softmax subtracts the row max for stability (matches torch).
52	  * CrossEntropy is MEAN over B: dlogits = (softmax - onehot) / B.
53	
54	This file imports torch only; it needs NO GPU and NO built extension.
55	"""
56	
57	from __future__ import annotations
58	
59	import math
60	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
61	from typing import Dict, List, Tuple
62	
63	import torch
64	
65	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
66	# Architecture constants (single source — mirrored by the C++ layout header and
67	# the codegen). These are the decoder cell's fixed shapes in the grokking race.
68	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
69	VOCAB = 99      # num_tokens (DEFAULT_CONFIG["num_tokens"]) — token range [0,98]
70	D_MODEL = 128   # dim_model (MODEL_SCALES["small"])
71	N_HEADS = 4     # num_heads
72	N_LAYERS = 2    # num_layers
73	SEQ = 4         # _raw_model hardcodes seq=4 for the decoder (make_data → 4 toks)
74	D_FF = 4 * D_MODEL  # 512 — ff hidden (Linear(d,4*d))
75	D_HEAD = D_MODEL // N_HEADS  # 32
76	LN_EPS = 1e-5   # torch.nn.LayerNorm default eps
77	ATTN_SCALE = 1.0 / math.sqrt(D_HEAD)  # 1/sqrt(32)
78	
79	
80	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
81	# Exact-erf GELU and its derivative (the REAL nn.GELU(), NOT the tanh approx).
82	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
83	_INV_SQRT2 = 1.0 / math.sqrt(2.0)
84	_INV_SQRT_2PI = 1.0 / math.sqrt(2.0 * math.pi)
85	
86	
87	def gelu(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
88	    return 0.5 * x * (1.0 + torch.erf(x * _INV_SQRT2))
89	
90	
91	def gelu_grad(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
92	    # d/dx [0.5 x (1+erf(x/sqrt2))] = 0.5(1+erf(x/sqrt2)) + x * phi(x),
93	    # phi(x) = (1/sqrt(2pi)) exp(-x^2/2)  (the normal pdf).
94	    cdf = 0.5 * (1.0 + torch.erf(x * _INV_SQRT2))
95	    pdf = _INV_SQRT_2PI * torch.exp(-0.5 * x * x)
96	    return cdf + x * pdf
97	
98	
99	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
100	# LayerNorm fwd/bwd (eps=1e-5), over the last dim (size d). Affine (gamma,beta).
101	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
102	def layernorm_forward(x, gamma, beta, eps=LN_EPS):
103	    """x: [..., d]. Returns (y, cache) where cache has the bwd intermediates."""
104	    mu = x.mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
105	    xc = x - mu
106	    var = (xc * xc).mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
107	    inv_std = 1.0 / torch.sqrt(var + eps)
108	    xhat = xc * inv_std
109	    y = xhat * gamma + beta
110	    return y, (xhat, inv_std, gamma)
111	
112	
113	def layernorm_backward(dy, cache):
114	    """Returns (dx, dgamma, dbeta). dgamma/dbeta summed over all but last dim."""
115	    xhat, inv_std, gamma = cache
116	    d = xhat.shape[-1]
117	    # Reduce gamma/beta grads over every leading (batch/seq) axis.
118	    reduce_axes = tuple(range(dy.dim() - 1))
119	    dbeta = dy.sum(dim=reduce_axes)
120	    dgamma = (dy * xhat).sum(dim=reduce_axes)
121	    dxhat = dy * gamma
122	    # Standard LN dx: (1/d) * inv_std * (d*dxhat - sum(dxhat) - xhat*sum(dxhat*xhat))
123	    sum_dxhat = dxhat.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
124	    sum_dxhat_xhat = (dxhat * xhat).sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
125	    dx = inv_std * (dxhat - (sum_dxhat + xhat * sum_dxhat_xhat) / d)
126	    return dx, dgamma, dbeta
127	
128	
129	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
130	# Softmax over the last dim with row-max subtraction (matches torch), + bwd.
131	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
132	def softmax_lastdim(x):
133	    m = x.max(dim=-1, keepdim=True).values
134	    e = torch.exp(x - m)
135	    s = e.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
136	    return e / s
137	
138	
139	def softmax_backward(dy, y):
140	    # dx = y * (dy - sum(dy*y))  (over the softmax axis).
141	    s = (dy * y).sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
142	    return y * (dy - s)
143	
144	
145	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
146	# Parameter container — mirrors named_parameters() ORDER exactly (30 tensors).
147	# The CUDA flat-buffer offsets are generated from this same order (see
148	# decoder_param_layout()).
149	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
150	# (name, shape) in the EXACT order torch's named_parameters() yields them. This
151	# is THE single source of truth for the flat weight layout; the C++ header
152	# (csrc/fused/sm_90/decoder_layout.cuh) static-asserts the count + total.
153	def decoder_param_spec() -> List[Tuple[str, Tuple[int, ...]]]:
154	    spec: List[Tuple[str, Tuple[int, ...]]] = [
155	        ("tok.weight", (VOCAB, D_MODEL)),
156	        ("pos.weight", (SEQ, D_MODEL)),
157	    ]
158	    for li in range(N_LAYERS):
159	        p = f"layers.{li}."
160	        spec += [
161	            (p + "attn.in_proj_weight", (3 * D_MODEL, D_MODEL)),
162	            (p + "attn.in_proj_bias", (3 * D_MODEL,)),
163	            (p + "attn.out_proj.weight", (D_MODEL, D_MODEL)),
164	            (p + "attn.out_proj.bias", (D_MODEL,)),
165	            (p + "n1.weight", (D_MODEL,)),
166	            (p + "n1.bias", (D_MODEL,)),
167	            (p + "n2.weight", (D_MODEL,)),
168	            (p + "n2.bias", (D_MODEL,)),
169	            (p + "ff.0.weight", (D_FF, D_MODEL)),
170	            (p + "ff.0.bias", (D_FF,)),
171	            (p + "ff.2.weight", (D_MODEL, D_FF)),
172	            (p + "ff.2.bias", (D_MODEL,)),
173	        ]
174	    spec += [
175	        ("norm.weight", (D_MODEL,)),
176	        ("norm.bias", (D_MODEL,)),
177	        ("out.weight", (VOCAB, D_MODEL)),
178	        ("out.bias", (VOCAB,)),
179	    ]
180	    return spec
181	
182	
183	def decoder_param_layout() -> Dict[str, object]:
184	    """Flat-buffer layout: offsets/sizes per tensor (the megakernel ABI view).
185	
186	    Returns dict with: names, offsets (elements into the flat buffer), sizes,
187	    total (== 422755), n_tensors (== 30). The offsets follow named_parameters()
188	    order so the flat blob == torch.cat([p.reshape(-1) for _, p in
189	    model.named_parameters()]).
190	    """
191	    spec = decoder_param_spec()
192	    names, offsets, sizes = [], [], []
193	    off = 0
194	    for name, shape in spec:
195	        n = 1
196	        for s in shape:
197	            n *= s
198	        names.append(name)
199	        offsets.append(off)
200	        sizes.append(n)
201	        off += n
202	    return dict(names=names, offsets=offsets, sizes=sizes, shapes=[s for _, s in spec],
203	                total=off, n_tensors=len(spec))
204	
205	
206	@dataclass
207	class DecoderWeights:
208	    """All 30 decoder weights as named tensors. Built either from a flat buffer
209	    (the megakernel view) or from a torch nn module's named_parameters()."""
210	    tok: torch.Tensor
211	    pos: torch.Tensor
212	    layers: List[Dict[str, torch.Tensor]]
213	    norm_w: torch.Tensor
214	    norm_b: torch.Tensor
215	    out_w: torch.Tensor
216	    out_b: torch.Tensor
217	
218	    @staticmethod
219	    def from_named(named: Dict[str, torch.Tensor]) -> "DecoderWeights":
220	        layers = []
221	        for li in range(N_LAYERS):
222	            p = f"layers.{li}."
223	            layers.append(dict(
224	                in_w=named[p + "attn.in_proj_weight"],
225	                in_b=named[p + "attn.in_proj_bias"],
226	                out_w=named[p + "attn.out_proj.weight"],
227	                out_b=named[p + "attn.out_proj.bias"],
228	                n1_w=named[p + "n1.weight"], n1_b=named[p + "n1.bias"],
229	                n2_w=named[p + "n2.weight"], n2_b=named[p + "n2.bias"],
230	                ff0_w=named[p + "ff.0.weight"], ff0_b=named[p + "ff.0.bias"],
231	                ff2_w=named[p + "ff.2.weight"], ff2_b=named[p + "ff.2.bias"],
232	            ))
233	        return DecoderWeights(
234	            tok=named["tok.weight"], pos=named["pos.weight"], layers=layers,
235	            norm_w=named["norm.weight"], norm_b=named["norm.bias"],
236	            out_w=named["out.weight"], out_b=named["out.bias"])
237	
238	    @staticmethod
239	    def from_flat(flat: torch.Tensor) -> "DecoderWeights":
240	        lay = decoder_param_layout()
241	        named = {}
242	        for name, off, sz, shape in zip(lay["names"], lay["offsets"],
243	                                        lay["sizes"], lay["shapes"]):
244	            named[name] = flat[off:off + sz].reshape(shape)
245	        return DecoderWeights.from_named(named)
246	
247	
248	def _causal_mask(seq: int, device, dtype) -> torch.Tensor:
249	    """Additive mask [seq, seq]: 0 where j<=i, -inf where j>i (triu diag=1)."""
250	    m = torch.triu(torch.ones(seq, seq, dtype=torch.bool, device=device), 1)
251	    add = torch.zeros(seq, seq, device=device, dtype=dtype)
252	    add = add.masked_fill(m, float("-inf"))
253	    return add
254	
255	
256	# ===========================================================================
257	#  FORWARD (manual, primitive ops) — caches everything the manual backward needs.
258	# ===========================================================================
259	def decoder_forward(W: DecoderWeights, tokens: torch.Tensor,
260	                    targets: torch.Tensor):
261	    """tokens: [B, SEQ] int64 in [0, VOCAB). targets: [B] int64.
262	
263	    Returns (loss_scalar, cache). loss = mean-over-batch cross-entropy on the
264	    LAST-position logits. cache holds every fwd intermediate for the backward.
265	    """
266	    B, S = tokens.shape
267	    device, dtype = W.tok.device, W.tok.dtype
268	    add_mask = _causal_mask(S, device, dtype)  # [S,S]
269	
270	    # Embedding + positional. pos_ids = arange(S).
271	    pos_ids = torch.arange(S, device=device)
272	    h = W.tok[tokens] + W.pos[pos_ids].unsqueeze(0)   # [B,S,d]
273	
274	    layer_caches = []
275	    for li in range(N_LAYERS):
276	        L = W.layers[li]
277	        x_in = h  # residual base for the attention sublayer
278	        # ----- self-attention (MultiheadAttention semantics) -----
279	        qkv = x_in @ L["in_w"].t() + L["in_b"]        # [B,S,3d]
280	        q, k, v = qkv.split(D_MODEL, dim=-1)
281	        # split heads: [B,S,d] -> [B,h,S,dh]
282	        def sh(t):
283	            return t.reshape(B, S, N_HEADS, D_HEAD).permute(0, 2, 1, 3)
284	        qh, kh, vh = sh(q), sh(k), sh(v)
285	        scores = (qh @ kh.transpose(-2, -1)) * ATTN_SCALE   # [B,h,S,S]
286	        scores = scores + add_mask                          # causal
287	        attn = softmax_lastdim(scores)                      # [B,h,S,S]
288	        ctxh = attn @ vh                                     # [B,h,S,dh]
289	        ctx = ctxh.permute(0, 2, 1, 3).reshape(B, S, D_MODEL)  # merge heads
290	        a = ctx @ L["out_w"].t() + L["out_b"]               # [B,S,d]
291	        # ----- residual + n1 (POST-LN): x = n1(x_in + a) -----
292	        r1 = x_in + a
293	        x1, ln1_cache = layernorm_forward(r1, L["n1_w"], L["n1_b"])
294	        # ----- FFN: ff2(gelu(ff0(x1))) -----
295	        ff0 = x1 @ L["ff0_w"].t() + L["ff0_b"]              # [B,S,4d]
296	        g = gelu(ff0)                                        # [B,S,4d]
297	        ff2 = g @ L["ff2_w"].t() + L["ff2_b"]              # [B,S,d]
298	        # ----- residual + n2 (POST-LN): h = n2(x1 + ff2) -----
299	        r2 = x1 + ff2
300	        h2, ln2_cache = layernorm_forward(r2, L["n2_w"], L["n2_b"])
301	        layer_caches.append(dict(
302	            x_in=x_in, qkv=qkv, qh=qh, kh=kh, vh=vh, attn=attn, ctxh=ctxh,
303	            ctx=ctx, r1=r1, x1=x1, ln1_cache=ln1_cache, ff0=ff0, g=g, r2=r2,
304	            ln2_cache=ln2_cache))
305	        h = h2
306	
307	    # Final norm + head on the LAST position only.
308	    h_last = h[:, -1, :]                                   # [B,d]
309	    hn, norm_cache = layernorm_forward(h_last, W.norm_w, W.norm_b)
310	    logits = hn @ W.out_w.t() + W.out_b                    # [B,VOCAB]
311	    # Cross-entropy, mean over batch (numerically-stable log-softmax).
312	    m = logits.max(dim=-1, keepdim=True).values
313	    logz = m.squeeze(-1) + torch.log(torch.exp(logits - m).sum(dim=-1))
314	    nll = logz - logits.gather(1, targets.unsqueeze(1)).squeeze(1)
315	    loss = nll.mean()
316	    cache = dict(B=B, S=S, tokens=tokens, targets=targets,
317	                 layer_caches=layer_caches, h_last=h_last, hn=hn,
318	                 norm_cache=norm_cache, logits=logits, add_mask=add_mask)
319	    return loss, cache
320	
321	
322	# ===========================================================================
323	#  BACKWARD (manual, NO autograd) — returns grads for every named parameter.
324	# ===========================================================================
325	def decoder_backward(W: DecoderWeights, cache) -> Dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
326	    B, S = cache["B"], cache["S"]
327	    targets = cache["targets"]
328	    tokens = cache["tokens"]
329	    grads: Dict[str, torch.Tensor] = {}
330	
331	    # ----- CE backward: dlogits = (softmax - onehot) / B -----
332	    logits = cache["logits"]
333	    sm = softmax_lastdim(logits)                           # [B,VOCAB]
334	    onehot = torch.zeros_like(sm)
335	    onehot.scatter_(1, targets.unsqueeze(1), 1.0)
336	    dlogits = (sm - onehot) / B                            # [B,VOCAB]
337	
338	    # ----- head (out): logits = hn @ out_w^T + out_b -----
339	    hn = cache["hn"]                                       # [B,d]
340	    grads["out.weight"] = dlogits.t() @ hn                 # [VOCAB,d]
341	    grads["out.bias"] = dlogits.sum(dim=0)                 # [VOCAB]
342	    dhn = dlogits @ W.out_w                                # [B,d]
343	
344	    # ----- final norm backward -----
345	    dh_last, dnorm_w, dnorm_b = layernorm_backward(dhn, cache["norm_cache"])
346	    grads["norm.weight"] = dnorm_w
347	    grads["norm.bias"] = dnorm_b
348	
349	    # Upstream into the last layer's output: only the LAST position has grad.
350	    dh = torch.zeros(B, S, D_MODEL, device=hn.device, dtype=hn.dtype)
351	    dh[:, -1, :] = dh_last
352	
353	    # ----- per-layer backward (reverse) -----
354	    for li in reversed(range(N_LAYERS)):
355	        L = W.layers[li]
356	        lc = cache["layer_caches"][li]
357	        gp = f"layers.{li}."
358	        # h2 = n2(r2);  dh is grad wrt h2.
359	        dr2, dn2_w, dn2_b = layernorm_backward(dh, lc["ln2_cache"])
360	        grads[gp + "n2.weight"] = dn2_w
361	        grads[gp + "n2.bias"] = dn2_b
362	        # r2 = x1 + ff2  -> grad flows to x1 (residual) AND ff2.
363	        dff2 = dr2
364	        dx1 = dr2.clone()
365	        # ff2 = g @ ff2_w^T + ff2_b
366	        g = lc["g"]                                        # [B,S,4d]
367	        grads[gp + "ff.2.weight"] = (dff2.reshape(-1, D_MODEL).t()
368	                                     @ g.reshape(-1, D_FF))   # [d,4d]
369	        grads[gp + "ff.2.bias"] = dff2.reshape(-1, D_MODEL).sum(dim=0)
370	        dg = dff2 @ W.layers[li]["ff2_w"]                  # [B,S,4d]
371	        # gelu backward
372	        dff0 = dg * gelu_grad(lc["ff0"])                   # [B,S,4d]
373	        # ff0 = x1 @ ff0_w^T + ff0_b
374	        x1 = lc["x1"]
375	        grads[gp + "ff.0.weight"] = (dff0.reshape(-1, D_FF).t()
376	                                     @ x1.reshape(-1, D_MODEL))  # [4d,d]
377	        grads[gp + "ff.0.bias"] = dff0.reshape(-1, D_FF).sum(dim=0)
378	        dx1 = dx1 + dff0 @ W.layers[li]["ff0_w"]           # add FFN path to x1
379	        # x1 = n1(r1) -> backward
380	        dr1, dn1_w, dn1_b = layernorm_backward(dx1, lc["ln1_cache"])
381	        grads[gp + "n1.weight"] = dn1_w
382	        grads[gp + "n1.bias"] = dn1_b
383	        # r1 = x_in + a -> grad to x_in (residual) AND a (attention out).
384	        da = dr1
385	        dx_in = dr1.clone()
386	        # a = ctx @ out_w^T + out_b
387	        ctx = lc["ctx"]                                    # [B,S,d]
388	        grads[gp + "attn.out_proj.weight"] = (da.reshape(-1, D_MODEL).t()
389	                                              @ ctx.reshape(-1, D_MODEL))
390	        grads[gp + "attn.out_proj.bias"] = da.reshape(-1, D_MODEL).sum(dim=0)
391	        dctx = da @ W.layers[li]["out_w"]                  # [B,S,d]
392	        # merge-heads backward: ctx[B,S,d] <- ctxh[B,h,S,dh]
393	        dctxh = dctx.reshape(B, S, N_HEADS, D_HEAD).permute(0, 2, 1, 3)  # [B,h,S,dh]
394	        # ctxh = attn @ vh
395	        attn = lc["attn"]; vh = lc["vh"]; qh = lc["qh"]; kh = lc["kh"]
396	        dattn = dctxh @ vh.transpose(-2, -1)               # [B,h,S,S]
397	        dvh = attn.transpose(-2, -1) @ dctxh               # [B,h,S,dh]

CUDA decoder megakernel (csrc/fused/sm_90/model_stages_decoder.cuh).

WHY (the gate the math-oracle cannot provide): decoder_oracle.py proves the
decoder fwd/bwd MATH is correct (matched to autograd ~1e-15). It does NOT
exercise the CUDA kernel's *structure* — the smem buffer reuse/aliasing, the
recompute-in-backward, the head-split index arithmetic, the owner-thread grad
accumulation, the per-sample sequential reduction. That structure is exactly
where a hand-written, un-runnable backward hides missing terms / index bugs /
dead-buffer reads (e.g. an attention dv term computed from an already-overwritten
softmax weight).

This module re-implements the kernel ALGORITHM in plain Python — same buffers
(as numpy/torch arrays), same aliasing decisions, same loop nests and index math,

the STRUCTURAL bug class. It is single-threaded, so it does NOT catch

guards — see the kernel header comments); it DOES catch everything else.

dec_recompute_layer, dec_backward_sample, dec_linear/_bwd, dec_layernorm_*,

def mirror_loss_and_grads(named_params: Dict[str, torch.Tensor],
                          tokens: torch.Tensor, targets: torch.Tensor):
    """Run the STRUCTURAL kernel mirror over the whole (small) batch.

    Mirrors the CTA loop: per sample, forward then immediately backward,
    accumulating weight grads into one partial (here a single CTA == whole batch,
    which is what determinism requires per element). Returns (loss, grads)."""
    named = {k: v.to(_F64) for k, v in named_params.items()}
    W = DecoderWeights.from_named(named)
    lay = decoder_param_layout()
    g = {name: torch.zeros(shape, dtype=_F64)
         for name, shape in zip(lay["names"], lay["shapes"])}
    B = tokens.shape[0]
    nll_sum = 0.0
    for b in range(B):
        tok_s = [int(tokens[b, s]) for s in range(SEQ)]
        tgt = int(targets[b])
        sm = _forward_sample(W, tok_s, tgt)
        logits = sm["logits"]
        mx = logits.max().item()
        es = sum(math.exp(logits[o].item() - mx) for o in range(VOCAB))
        nll_sum += (mx + math.log(es)) - logits[tgt].item()
        _backward_sample(W, g, tok_s, tgt, B, sm)
    return nll_sum / B, g

def fused_training_step(
    optimizer: MegakernelOptimizer,
    loss: "torch.Tensor",
    framework_backward: Optional[Callable[["torch.Tensor"], None]] = None,
) -> None:
    """Reference glue for one fused-aware training step (§8.4 control flow).

    Encapsulates the backward/step reconciliation so a framework loop (or the
    test harness) can call a single function:

        1. Ask the hook whether the fused kernel owns backward.
        2. If not (L0/L1), run ``framework_backward(loss)`` (the engine's
           autograd backward).

           (already applied) and the real step for L0/L1.

    ``framework_backward`` defaults to ``loss.backward`` when not supplied.
    """
    if not optimizer.backward(loss):
        bwd = framework_backward or (lambda x: x.backward())
        bwd(loss)
    optimizer.step()
